leads.title: Romer v. Evans - U.S. Supreme Court (1996)
leads.documents: Struck down Colorado Initiative 2 (1992 constitutional amendment) that prohibited protected status for homosexual, lesbian or bisexual orientation; holds amendment was motivated by animus and violated Equal Protection Clause of Fourteenth Amendment.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 1994 Colorado Supreme Court found amendment unconstitutional; 1996 U.S. Supreme Court held in Romer v. Evans amendment 'allows discrimination against homosexuals and prevents the state from protecting them'.

leads.title: Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission / Craig v. Masterpiece Cakeshop
leads.documents: Enforcement of Colorado anti-discrimination public-accommodations machinery; gay couple refused wedding cake in Lakewood in June 2012, won before Administrative Law Judge Robert N. Spencer Dec 6, then ruling thrown out 7-2 by U.S. Supreme Court June 2018 in favor of bakery.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: Craig v. Masterpiece Cakeshop (ALJ decision) and Masterpiece Cakeshop v. Colorado Civil Rights Commission (SCOTUS June 2018).

leads.title: Chiles v. Salazar - U.S. Supreme Court (March 31, 2026) and HB 26-1322
leads.documents: Constitutionality of Colorado conversion-therapy ban on minors (signed May 31, 2019 by Gov. Jared Polis); 10th Circuit upheld, SCOTUS agreed March 10, 2025 to hear challenge, ruled 8-1 March 31, 2026 that ban must face strict scrutiny as viewpoint discrimination; Colorado responded May 8, 2026 with HB 26-1322 redefining conversion therapy as direction to pre-determined outcome and removing statute of limitations.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: Chiles v. Salazar, 8-1 vote; HB 26-1322 passed May 8, 2026.

leads.title: McDaniel-Miccio v. Hickenlooper + marriage equality orders (2014)
leads.documents: State-court challenge to Colorado marriage definition arguing civil unions created second-class citizenship; led to Oct 6-7, 2014 dismissal of appeal/lift of stay after 10th Circuit Oklahoma/Utah precedents, Colorado Supreme Court lifted barriers, AG John Suthers ordered clerks to issue licenses; plus Jan 2021 Colorado Supreme Court retroactive recognition of pre-2014 common-law same-sex marriages.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: Filed Feb 19, 2014 by nine same-sex couples; defendants Gov. Hickenlooper and Denver City Clerk; AG John Suthers.

leads.title: Colorado Anti-Discrimination Act - 2008 amendment and Kelly Loving Act (May 2025)
leads.documents: Statewide ban on discrimination on basis of sexual orientation and gender identity or expression in employment, housing, public accommodations, education, credit since 2008; defines 'sexual orientation' to include transgender status/perception; strengthened for transgender Coloradans by Kelly Loving Act signed May 2025 by Gov. Jared Polis.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: category 'sexual orientation' added 2008, signed by Gov. Bill Ritter; Kelly Loving Act signed May 2025.

leads.title: Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment / Division of Motor Vehicles - gender marker rules
leads.documents: Removal Feb 2019 of surgery requirement for gender change (required Jan 1, 1984 to Feb 13, 2019); current process by request via 'Change of Sex Designation' form for DL/state ID and 'Birth Certificate Correction Form' + 'Sex Designation Form' for birth certificate; minors need parent/guardian + medical/mental health professional consent; descriptors M/F/Intersex/X for birth certificates, male/female/X for IDs.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: unanimous board vote Feb 2019.

leads.title: Colorado gender-affirming healthcare protections - 2021 insurance mandate and April 2023 shield law
leads.documents: Announced Oct 2021 that from 2023 basic health insurance must include sexual reassignment surgery as human right/basic policy - first in U.S.; April 2023 General Assembly and Governor passed/signed legislation to protect, defend and guarantee gender-affirming healthcare and 'safe passage of transgender individuals from interstate'.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: passed/signed April 2023; implemented legislation.

leads.title: Colorado Civil Rights Division - Coy Mathis ruling (2013) / Growing Up Coy (2016 film)
leads.documents: Landmark 2013 ruling in favor of transgender six-year-old Coy Mathis to use girls' bathroom at elementary school in Fountain, Colorado; credited with setting off wave of bathroom bills; plus 2023 Colorado law allowing full access to bathroom facilities for all genders.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: 2016 film Growing Up Coy documented case.

leads.title: Movement Advancement Project - Colorado's Equality Profile
leads.documents: LGBT think-tank ranking of LGBTQ rights legislation; ranks Colorado second in Mountain West region behind Nevada; cited as evidence Colorado frequently referred to as one of most LGBT-friendly states in Mountain West.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Listed in External links as: Colorado's Equality Profile - via the Movement Advancement Project; LGBT Rights in Colorado - via Equaldex.

leads.title: Colorado hate-crime enforcement - 2001 law, 2009 Greeley transgender murder conviction, Club Q shooting 2022
leads.documents: Hate-crime law protections based on sexual orientation and gender identity/expression since 2001 with penalty enhancements; 2009 Greeley jury convicted man of first-degree murder as hate crime in transgender victim case - thought first applied in murder trial; Nov 2022 mass shooting at gay bar in Colorado Springs (Club Q), 305 charges, FBI investigation, red-flag law lawsuit, April 2023 emergency gun bills; reported 380% increase in sexual-orientation hate crimes since 2018.
leads.detail: No URL visible. Cited as: Greeley conviction 2009; Colorado Springs shooting Nov 2022; Dec 2022 charges; April 2023 gun laws signed; June 2023 lawsuit against Sheriff's Department.
